title: The symmetric algebra of a finitely presented module is a finitely presented algebra, generated by generators of the module
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-module, with symmetric algebra $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\operatorname{Sym}^n_R(M)$ and its canonical $R$-linear map $\iota_M:M\to\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property] (the inclusion $M=\operatorname{Sym}^1_R(M)\subseteq\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$). (a) If $m_1,\dots,m_n$ generate $M$ as an $R$-module, then $\iota_M(m_1),\dots,\iota_M(m_n)$ generate $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ as an $R$-algebra. (b) If $M$ is a finitely presented $R$-module (there is an exact sequence $R^{\oplus m}\to R^{\oplus n}\to M\to0$, Stacks, Algebra, Definition 0518), then $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra (isomorphic to $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(g_1,\dots,g_m)$ with $g_1,\dots,g_m$ linear forms); and then for every finitely generated ideal $\mathfrak a\subseteq\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ the quotient $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)/\mathfrak a$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra.

source.place: Algebra, Section 00DM (section-tensor-algebra) and Lemma 00DO (lemma-presentation-sym-exterior, line 2241: for M_2 -> M_1 -> M -> 0 exact, M_2 (x) Sym^{n-1}(M_1) -> Sym^n(M_1) -> Sym^n(M) -> 0 is exact, so with M_1 = R^n, Sym(M) = R[x_1..x_n]/(linear forms of the relations)); the quotient by a finitely generated ideal: Algebra, Lemma 00R2 (lemma-finite-presentation-independent, line 566) and the definition of finite presentation; used in Properties, Lemmas 05JS, 086N, 0817 ('A_{i,j} is a quasi-coherent finitely presented O_X-algebra')

proof.text: (a), the image of $M$ generates.) Let $B\subseteq\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ be the $R$-subalgebra generated by $\iota_M(M)$, $j:B\to\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ the inclusion and $\iota':M\to B$ the corestriction of $\iota_M$, so $j\circ\iota'=\iota_M$. $B$ is a commutative $R$-algebra (a subalgebra of the commutative $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$), so by the universal property [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property] there is an $R$-algebra homomorphism $g:\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)\to B$ with $g\circ\iota_M=\iota'$. Then $j\circ g$ and $\operatorname{id}$ are $R$-algebra endomorphisms of $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ with $(j\circ g)\circ\iota_M=j\circ\iota'=\iota_M=\operatorname{id}\circ\iota_M$, so $j\circ g=\operatorname{id}$ by the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. Hence $j$ is surjective, i.e. $B=\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$. (Equivalently, Stacks 00DM: $\operatorname{Sym}^n(M)$ is generated by the products $x_1\cdots x_n$ of elements of $M$.)

source.place: Algebra, Section 00DM (section-tensor-algebra, line 2213: the images x_1...x_n of pure tensors generate Sym^n(M))

proof.text: (a), conclusion.) If $m_1,\dots,m_n$ generate $M$, every $x\in M$ is $\sum_i r_im_i$ with $r_i\in R$, so $\iota_M(x)=\sum_ir_i\iota_M(m_i)$ by $R$-linearity of $\iota_M$ lies in the $R$-subalgebra $R[\iota_M(m_1),\dots,\iota_M(m_n)]$. This subalgebra therefore contains $\iota_M(M)$, hence contains the subalgebra generated by $\iota_M(M)$, which is $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ by Step 1. So the $\iota_M(m_i)$ generate $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ as an $R$-algebra; equivalently the $R$-algebra map $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$, $x_i\mapsto\iota_M(m_i)$, is surjective.

source.place: Algebra, Section 00DM (section-tensor-algebra); Definition 0518 (definition-module-finite-type, line 349) for generators of a module

proof.text: (b), $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ as a quotient of $\operatorname{Sym}_R(R^{\oplus n})$.) Let $M$ be finitely presented: there is an exact sequence $R^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{\alpha}R^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{p}M\to0$ (Stacks, Algebra, Definition 0518). Write $F=R^{\oplus n}$ with standard basis $e_1,\dots,e_n$, $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_m$ the standard basis of $R^{\oplus m}$ and $\alpha(\varepsilon_j)=\sum_{i=1}^na_{ij}e_i$ ($a_{ij}\in R$). By exactness $p$ is surjective and $K:=\ker p=\operatorname{im}\alpha=\sum_jR\,\alpha(\varepsilon_j)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-quotient-module] the $R$-algebra map $\operatorname{Sym}(p):\operatorname{Sym}_R(F)\to\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ with $\iota_F(x)\mapsto\iota_M(p(x))$ is surjective with kernel the ideal $J$ generated by $\iota_F(K)$. Since $\iota_F$ is $R$-linear [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property], $\iota_F(K)=\sum_jR\,\iota_F(\alpha(\varepsilon_j))$, and an ideal contains this $R$-submodule iff it contains its generators; so $J=(\iota_F(\alpha(\varepsilon_1)),\dots,\iota_F(\alpha(\varepsilon_m)))$ and $\operatorname{Sym}(p)$ induces an $R$-algebra isomorphism $\operatorname{Sym}_R(F)/J\cong\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00DO (lemma-presentation-sym-exterior, line 2241) with M_1 = R^n, M_2 = R^m, summed over all degrees; Definition 0518 (line 349)

proof.text: (b), the explicit presentation.) By [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial] the $R$-algebra map $\varphi:\operatorname{Sym}_R(F)\to R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ with $\varphi(\iota_F(e_i))=x_i$ is an isomorphism; by $R$-linearity of $\iota_F$, $\varphi(\iota_F(\alpha(\varepsilon_j)))=\sum_ia_{ij}x_i=:\ell_j$, a linear form. A ring isomorphism carries the ideal generated by given elements onto the ideal generated by their images, so $\varphi(J)=(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_m)$ and, with Step 3, $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)\cong\operatorname{Sym}_R(F)/J\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_m)$ as $R$-algebras. By Stacks, Algebra, Definition 00F3 (with $f_j=g_j=\ell_j$), $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra. (Under this isomorphism $x_i\mapsto\iota_M(p(e_i))$, the generators of Step 2 for $m_i=p(e_i)$.)

source.place: Algebra, Section 00DM (line 2226: Sym(R^n) = R[x_1..x_n]) and Definition 00F3 (definition-finite-type, line 518)

proof.text: (b), quotients.) Let $\mathfrak a\subseteq\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ be a finitely generated ideal. Since $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra by Step 4, $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)/\mathfrak a$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-quotient-fg-ideal] (explicitly: lifting generators of $\mathfrak a$ to $h_1,\dots,h_k\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)/\mathfrak a\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_m,h_1,\dots,h_k)$).
